stem: Someone develops sudden stroke-like symptoms that disappear after a few minutes. Which of the following is the best interpretation?

options.label: A
options.text: The episode is harmless because the symptoms stopped
options.misconception: Resolution is being used to dismiss a brief but serious warning event.
options.explanation: The CDC warns that stroke-like symptoms resolving within minutes may be a TIA and still require medical help.

options.label: B
options.text: The episode matters only if the symptoms return the same day
options.misconception: A recurrence requirement is being invented before a warning event is taken seriously.
options.explanation: The cited warning does not require a second episode; even one brief episode of stroke-like symptoms may be a TIA.

options.label: C
options.text: The episode can be ignored if speech has returned to normal
options.misconception: Recovery of one function is being used to erase the significance of the earlier stroke-like symptoms.
options.explanation: Complete symptom resolution does not make the episode safe to ignore; the CDC identifies this pattern as a possible TIA.

options.label: D
options.text: The episode needs attention only if it lasted more than one hour
options.misconception: An unsupported duration threshold is being used to dismiss symptoms that resolved within minutes.
options.explanation: The cited passage specifically warns that symptoms lasting only a few minutes may still indicate a TIA.

options.label: E
options.text: Treat the episode as a possible TIA needing medical help
options.misconception: None; brief resolving stroke symptoms can signal a TIA.
options.explanation: Stroke-like symptoms that disappear after a few minutes may represent a TIA. Their brevity does not make them harmless; medical help is still needed.

context: Learning objective: recognize a transient ischemic attack. Stroke-like deficits that clear within minutes can still be a serious ischemic warning and should not be ignored.
